No\. \(IB\) – __*\[\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\]*__/__*\[20\_\_\]* __IN THE MATTER OF:__ __M/s __*\[Name of Financial Creditor\]*__ Limited__ __…Financial Creditor__ __Versus__ __M/s __*\[Name of Corporate Debtor\]*__ Private Limited__ __…Corporate Debtor__ __STATUS REPORT ON THE PROGRESS OF THE CORPORATE INSOLVENCY__ __RESOLUTION PROCESS OF THE CORPORATE DEBTOR UNDER THE__ __INSOLVENCY AND BANKRUPTCY CODE, 2016 \(AS AMENDED UP TO 2026\)__ __Most Respectfully Showeth:__ 1. That this Status Report is being filed by the Resolution Professional on the progress of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process \(“CIRP”\) of the Corporate Debtor under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as amended from time to time, including by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code \(Amendment\) Act, 2026 \(Act No\. 6 of 2026\), and the regulations made thereunder\. 2. That this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority, vide its order dated *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*, was pleased to admit Company Petition C\.P\. No\. \(IB\) *\[\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\]*/*\[20\_\_\]*, filed by the Financial Creditor, M/s *\[Name of Financial Creditor\]* Limited, under Section 7 of the Code for initiating the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor, M/s *\[Name of Corporate Debtor\]* Private Limited\. By the said order, this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority also appointed the undersigned as the Interim Resolution Professional \(“IRP”\)\. The order was uploaded on the NCLT website on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]* and the certified copy was received by the IRP on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. A copy of the said order is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – A__\. 3. That the registered office and principal place of business of the Corporate Debtor is situated at: __Registered Office: __*\[Registered Office Address\]*, New Delhi\-*\[\_\_\_\_\_\_\]*\. 4. That the undersigned, in order to take custody and control of the assets and records of the Corporate Debtor, visited its registered office on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*; however, another company, namely M/s *\[Name of Other Entity\]*, was found operating at the said address, and no employee of the Corporate Debtor was available at the registered office address\. 5. That the undersigned thereafter contacted the members of the suspended Board of Directors of the Corporate Debtor through e\-mail, informed them of the commencement of the CIRP, and called upon them to provide access to all books of account, documents, and other records of the Corporate Debtor, as no records were found at its registered office\. Photographs of the premises of the registered office are annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – B \(Colly\)__\. 6. That in compliance with the admission order dated *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*, the undersigned, in the capacity of IRP, made a public announcement under Section 15 of the Code read with Regulation 6 of the IBBI \(Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons\) Regulations, 2016 \(“CIRP Regulations”\), which was published on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. A copy of the public announcement is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – C \(Colly\)__\. 7. That, upon collation and verification of the claims received, the undersigned constituted the Committee of Creditors \(“CoC”\) under Section 21\(1\) of the Code and filed a report certifying the constitution of the CoC before this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority under Regulation 17\(1\) of the CIRP Regulations on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. 8. That, the Corporate Debtor having a class of creditors \(Real Estate Allottees\), the undersigned, in the public announcement, offered a choice of three Insolvency Professionals to act as the Authorised Representative \(“AR”\) of the said class, in terms of Regulation 4A of the CIRP Regulations\. The Insolvency Professional who was the choice of the highest number of financial creditors in the class, namely *\[Name of Authorised Representative\]*, IBBI Regn\. No\. *\[IBBI/IPA\-\_\_\_/IP\-\_\_\_/\_\_\_\_\-\_\_/\_\_\_\_\_\]*, was accordingly selected, and the undersigned filed an application before this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority for the appointment of the said Authorised Representative of the class of financial creditors under Section 21\(6A\)\(b\) of the Code read with Regulation 16A of the CIRP Regulations on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. 9. That the First meeting of the CoC was convened on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*, wherein the CoC did not resolve to appoint the Resolution Professional\. In terms of Section 22\(3\)\(a\) of the Code and Regulation 17\(3\) of the CIRP Regulations, the undersigned has, in the absence of such appointment, continued to discharge the duties of the Resolution Professional from the fortieth day of the insolvency commencement date until a Resolution Professional is appointed\. A copy of the minutes of the First CoC meeting is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – D__\. 10. That the undersigned sent several reminders to the members of the suspended Board of Directors to hand over the books of account and the custody and control of the assets of the Corporate Debtor\. In response, the members of the suspended Board exchanged several e\-mails amongst themselves, each attributing responsibility to the other for furnishing the accounting data and records, and none of them furnished complete information, records, or custody and control of the assets; in one such e\-mail, uncertified accounting data by way of a Tally software backup was enclosed\. In view of such continued non\-cooperation, the undersigned has filed an application before this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority under Section 19\(2\) of the Code seeking necessary directions\. Copies of the e\-mails exchanged are annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – E \(Colly\)__\. 11. That the Second meeting of the CoC was convened on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*, wherein the CoC again did not resolve to appoint the Resolution Professional, and the undersigned has continued to discharge the duties of the Resolution Professional as aforesaid\. In the said meeting, the CoC considered the eligibility criteria for prospective resolution applicants, Form G \(Invitation for Expression of Interest\), the Request for Resolution Plan \(“RFRP”\), and the Evaluation Matrix, but did not approve any of the said matters\. A copy of the minutes of the Second CoC meeting is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – F__\. 12. That the undersigned received an e\-mail dated *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]* from a member of the CoC, M/s *\[Name of Assignor Creditor\]* Limited, intimating the assignment of its debt to M/s *\[Name of Assignee Creditor\]* Limited vide assignment deed dated *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*; the assignee thereafter filed Form C under Regulation 8 of the CIRP Regulations on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. The undersigned reconstituted the CoC accordingly and, on the request of the members, convened the Third meeting of the CoC on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*\. In the Third CoC meeting, the CoC resolved to appoint the undersigned as the Resolution Professional — the undersigned being, by virtue of Section 22\(3\)\(a\) of the Code, deemed appointed from the date of the said resolution — and also approved the eligibility criteria for prospective resolution applicants, Form G, the RFRP, and the Evaluation Matrix\. A copy of the minutes of the Third CoC meeting is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – G__\. 13. That the undersigned, as Resolution Professional, issued Form G – Invitation for Expression of Interest from prospective resolution applicants under Regulation 36A of the CIRP Regulations on *\[DD\.MM\.20\_\_\]*, which was published in *\[Hindi\-language daily\]* \(Hindi edition\) and *\[English\-language daily\]* \(English edition\)\. A copy of Form G is annexed herewith and marked as __Annexure – H__\. 14. That the undersigned Resolution Professional most respectfully prays that this Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority may be pleased to take the present Status Report on the progress of the CIRP of the Corporate Debtor on record, and pass such further order\(s\) as it may deem fit in the interest of justice\. Key changes reflected: __Provision__ __Position reflected in this template \(as amended up to 2026\)__ __Sec\. 7\(5\) / 9\(5\) / 10\(4\)__ Admission of the application is now mandatory — the Adjudicating Authority “shall” admit within 14 days where default and statutory compliance are established; reasons must be recorded in writing for any delay beyond 14 days \(IBC Amendment Act, 2026\)\. __Sec\. 21\(6A\)\(b\) r/w Reg\. 4A & 16A__ Corrected citation for the Authorised Representative of a class of creditors\. The IRP offers a choice of at least three IPs in the public announcement \(Reg\. 4A\) and the IP who is the choice of the highest number of financial creditors in the class is selected as AR and placed before the AA for appointment \(Reg\. 16A\)\. The earlier draft’s reference to “Regulation 8A\(3\)” has been replaced\. __Sec\. 22\(3\)\(a\) \[amended 2026\]__ Where the CoC resolves to appoint the RP, the RP is now deemed appointed from the date of the CoC resolution, and the decision is to be communicated to the insolvency professional, the Corporate Debtor and the IBBI\. __Reg\. 17\(1\) & 17\(3\)__ Report certifying constitution of the CoC to be filed within 30 days of appointment \(Reg\. 17\(1\)\); where appointment of the RP is delayed, the IRP shall continue to act as RP from the 40th day of the insolvency commencement date until the RP is appointed \(Reg\. 17\(3\)\)\. __Sec\. 19\(2\)__ Application for directions against non\-cooperating personnel / suspended management retained — provision unchanged in substance\. __Sec\. 12A \[substituted 2026\]__ Withdrawal of an admitted application is permitted only after constitution of the CoC and before issuance of the first invitation for resolution plans, with approval of 90% of the CoC voting share\. \(Relevant where a Sec\. 12A application arises during the process\.\) __Sec\. 240B / e\-filing__ Filings are progressively migrating to the electronic insolvency portal notified under the new Section 240B; the physical filing format is retained here pending full roll\-out\. *Note: Replace every \[bracketed\] field with case\-specific particulars before filing\. No\. \(IB\) – \[●\] \(ND\) / \[YYYY\]\.__ Respected Sir, That vide order dated \[Date of Admission Order\] passed by the Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority, New Delhi Bench \[●\] \(communicated on \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\]\), the undersigned has been appointed as the Interim Resolution Professional of the Corporate Debtor\. Accordingly, the undersigned respectfully submits the First Status Report along with the Report of Constitution of the Committee of Creditors, as under: __Date__ __Events__ \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The Hon’ble Adjudicating Authority, New Delhi Bench \[●\], vide its order dated \[Date of Admission Order\] \(communicated to the undersigned on \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\]\), initiated the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process \(“CIRP”\) against the Corporate Debtor and appointed the undersigned as the Interim Resolution Professional\. By virtue of the said order, a moratorium under Section 14 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 \(“the Code”, as amended, including by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code \(Amendment\) Act, 2026\) came into operation, and the powers of the Board of Directors of the Corporate Debtor stood suspended and vested in the Interim Resolution Professional in terms of Section 17 of the Code\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned invited quotations for engagement of advocate\(s\) for the Interim Resolution Professional and, accordingly, engaged \[Name of the Advocate\], Advocate, to represent the Interim Resolution Professional\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned filed his written communication / consent to act as the Interim Resolution Professional \(Form 2\) and made the requisite intimation on the electronic platform of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India \(Form CP\-1\), vide filing / diary no\. \[●\]\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned made the Public Announcement in Form A under Regulation 6 of the IBBI \(Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons\) Regulations, 2016 \(“CIRP Regulations”\), in the format notified by the Board, in \[English Newspaper\] \(English\) and \[Vernacular Newspaper\] \(\[language\]\), intimating the commencement of the CIRP and inviting claims from the creditors of the Corporate Debtor\. The copies thereof, along with the true typed copies, are annexed herewith as __Annexure\-1 \(Colly\)__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued e\-mails to the suspended directors intimating the initiation of the CIRP and sought certain preliminary information / documents, including provisional financials as on \[Date of Admission Order\]\. The copies of the said e\-mails are annexed herewith as __Annexure\-2 \(Colly\)__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued an e\-mail to the Operational Creditor, together with a reminder e\-mail dated \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\], for remittance of Rs\. \[●\]/\- as directed by the Hon’ble Tribunal in the admission order, towards the initial expenses to be incurred in the CIRP\. The copies of the said e\-mails are annexed herewith as __Annexure\-3 \(Colly\)__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned received an e\-mail from the suspended directors stating that the documents would be furnished upon re\-opening of office\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-4__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued an e\-mail to the Operational Creditor requesting it to file its claim and to release Rs\. \[●\]/\- towards the initial CIRP expenses\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-5__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued an e\-mail to the Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi, intimating the initiation of the CIRP against the Corporate Debtor\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued an e\-mail to the bankers of the Corporate Debtor intimating the initiation of the CIRP and requesting them to file their claim\. The copies of the e\-mails / correspondence exchanged with the bankers are annexed herewith as __Annexure\-6 \(Colly\)__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] During the CIRP, the undersigned learnt that an appeal against the admission order had been preferred by \[Name of the Suspended Director\], one of the suspended directors of the Corporate Debtor, before the Hon’ble National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi, bearing Comp\. App\. \(AT\) \(Ins\.\) No\. \[●\] of \[YYYY\], which was listed on \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\]\. The said appeal is pending and the next date of hearing is \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\]\. The copy of the order is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-7__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned issued a reminder e\-mail to the suspended directors requesting them to furnish the preliminary information / documents sought\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-8__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The undersigned filed the admission order in Form INC\-28 with the Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi & Haryana\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The suspended board of directors, vide their e\-mail, furnished part of the information / documents, including the balance sheet and income\-tax returns of the Corporate Debtor for the preceding three years\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-9__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The suspended directors, vide their e\-mail, requested the Interim Resolution Professional to approve certain payments / expenses to maintain the Corporate Debtor as a going concern\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-10__\. \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] The Interim Resolution Professional, vide his e\-mail, sought a detailed break\-up of the payments / expenses proposed and requested the suspended directors to apprise him of the authorised signatories of the bank account\(s\) maintained by the Corporate Debtor\. The copy of the said e\-mail is annexed herewith as __Annexure\-11__\. Despite the efforts made by the Interim Resolution Professional, no claim has been received from the creditors of the Corporate Debtor as on the date of this Report\. The Committee of Creditors has, accordingly, not been constituted till date\. *\[Where claims are received: the claims have been verified and the concerned creditor\(s\) informed of the acceptance / rejection thereof \(in whole or in part\) within seven days, as required under Regulation 13 of the CIRP Regulations \(as amended\), and the Report certifying constitution of the Committee of Creditors under Regulation 17 shall be filed accordingly\.\]* It is, accordingly, prayed that the above Status Report by the Interim Resolution Professional for the period \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\] to \[DD\.MM\.YYYY\], along with the Report of Constitution of the Committee of Creditors in the above\-captioned matter, be taken on record\. __\[Name of the Interim Resolution Professional\]__ Interim Resolution Professional \[Name of the Corporate Debtor\] Regn\. That the Annexures filed along with the present Status Report are true copies of their respective originals\. __DEPONENT__ __VERIFICATION__ Verified at \[Place\] on this \[●\] day of \[Month\], \[Year\] that the contents of the above affidavit are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, no part thereof is false and nothing material has been concealed therefrom\. __DEPONENT__ __DRAFTING NOTE__ *Statutory & Regulatory Position — as amended up to 2026* - __Governing framework: __This precedent reflects the position under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 as amended by the IBC \(Amendment\) Act, 2026 \(Act No\. 6 of 2026\) — Presidential assent dated 6 April 2026, with the specified provisions brought into force w\.e\.f\. 26 May 2026 \(S\.O\. 2625\(E\)\) — read with the IBBI \(CIRP\) Regulations, 2016 as amended up to the Fourth Amendment Regulations, 2026\. - __Moratorium: __The moratorium under Section 14 of the Code operates from the insolvency commencement date and continues for the duration prescribed; Background and Purpose - PPIRP was introduced by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code \(Amendment\) Ordinance promulgated on 4 April 2021, later enacted as the IBC \(Amendment\) Act, 2021, inserting Chapter III\-A into the Code\. The IBBI notified the PPIRP Regulations with effect from 9 April 2021\. - The trigger was the financial distress faced by micro, small and medium enterprises during the COVID\-19 disruption\. To cushion the sector, the Government had raised the minimum default for CIRP to ₹1 crore and suspended fresh CIRP filings for the period 25 March 2020 to 24 March 2021\. - MSMEs contribute a significant share of GDP, employment and exports\. Given the unique nature of their businesses and simpler corporate structures, a quicker, cost\-effective and value\-maximising resolution mechanism — least disruptive to business continuity and preserving jobs — was considered necessary\. - PPIRP is therefore a hybrid, “debtor\-in\-possession / creditor\-in\-control” process: management is largely retained while creditors approve a pre\-negotiated plan, with formal NCLT supervision compressing the timeline\. # 3\. Eligibility — Section 54A An application for PPIRP may be made only in respect of a corporate debtor that is an MSME and that satisfies the conditions in Section 54A\. The threshold question is MSME classification\. ## 4\.1 MSME classification \(revised w\.e\.f\. 1 April 2025\) A __composite criterion__ of both investment in plant and machinery / equipment __and__ annual turnover applies\. Both limits must be satisfied\. The thresholds were enhanced with effect from 1 April 2025: __Category__ __Investment in P&M / equipment__ __Annual turnover__ __Earlier limit \(to 31\-03\-2025\)__ Micro Up to ₹2\.5 crore Up to ₹10 crore ₹1 Cr / ₹5 Cr Small Up to ₹25 crore Up to ₹100 crore ₹10 Cr / ₹50 Cr Medium Up to ₹125 crore Up to ₹500 crore ₹50 Cr / ₹250 Cr *Source: Notification S\.O\. 1364\(E\) dated 21 March 2025 \(superseding S\.O\. 2119\(E\) dated 26 June 2020\)\. Classification is validated through Udyam Registration\.* ## 4\.2 How the composite test operates - Upward movement: if an enterprise crosses the ceiling on either criterion \(investment or turnover\), it moves to the next higher category\. - Reverse graduation: an enterprise drops to a lower category only if it falls below the ceilings on both criteria; it retains its existing status until the close of the financial year, with the benefit of the changed status from 1 April of the following year\. - Aggregation by PAN: all units with a GSTIN against the same PAN are treated as one enterprise; their investment and turnover are aggregated for classification\. ## 4\.3 Computing investment in plant and machinery / equipment - Linked to the Income\-tax Return \(ITR\) of prior years\. For a new enterprise with no ITR, investment is taken on the promoter’s self\-declaration; this relaxation ends after 31 March of the financial year in which the first ITR is filed\. - “Plant and machinery or equipment” carries the meaning in the Income\-tax Rules, 1962 and includes all tangible assets other than land and building, furniture and fittings\. - For a running unit with ITR and balance sheet, the written\-down \(depreciated\) value is considered; for a new unit without ITR, the purchase \(invoice\) value — first\-hand or second\-hand — is taken, excluding GST, on a self\-disclosure basis\. - Excluded from investment \(Explanation 1 to Section 7\(1\) of the MSMED Act\): cost of pollution control, research and development, industrial safety devices, and such other items as may be notified\. ## 4\.4 Computing turnover - Exports of goods or services are excluded while computing turnover for classification\. - Turnover and export figures are linked to the Income\-tax Act / CGST Act and the GSTIN\. PAN and GSTIN are mandatory; classification is validated through Udyam Registration\. ## 4\.5 Other eligibility conditions under Section 54A - Default of at least ₹10 lakh \(minimum threshold notified for PPIRP\)\. - The CD has not undergone CIRP or PPIRP, and no such process has been completed, in the three years preceding the initiation date\. - No liquidation order has been passed against the CD\. - The CD is eligible to submit a resolution plan under Section 29A\. \(Section 29A disqualifies, among others, an undischarged insolvent, a wilful defaulter, a person whose account is classified NPA, a person convicted of a punishable offence, a disqualified director, a person prohibited by SEBI, and a promoter of certain avoidance transactions\.\) Note: under Section 240A, clauses \(c\) and \(h\) of Section 29A do not apply to an MSME resolution applicant\. # 5\. Pre\-Initiation Steps and Approvals ## 5\.1 Proposing and approving the Resolution Professional — Section 54A\(2\)\(e\) - Financial creditors who are not related parties and hold at least 10% in value of the total financial debt may propose the name\(s\) of an insolvency professional to act as RP; FCs representing at least 66% in value approve the proposal, with the terms of appointment, in Form P3\. - Notice of the FC meeting is served on all unrelated FCs at least 5 days before the meeting \(a shorter period if all agree\) in Form P2, indicating the date, time, venue and the list of creditors with amounts due\. - Where there are no unrelated FCs \(or all FCs are related parties\), the corresponding provisions apply mutatis mutandis to the operational creditors\. ## 5\.2 Declaration, special resolution and creditor approval — Section 54A\(2\)\(f\)/\(g\) and 54A\(3\) - A majority of the directors / partners make a declaration in Form P6 stating that: \(i\) the CD will file the PPIRP application within a definite period not exceeding 90 days; \(ii\) PPIRP is not being initiated to defraud any person; and \(iii\) the name of the IP proposed and approved as RP\. - The members of the CD pass a special resolution approving the filing of the PPIRP application \(for a partnership, an equivalent resolution of at least three\-fourths of partners\)\. - The CD obtains approval of unrelated FCs representing at least 66% in value of the financial debt, in Form P4, for filing the application\. Where there are no unrelated FCs, approval of OCs is obtained\. - The CD furnishes to the FCs: the special resolution, the directors’/partners’ declaration \(Form P6\), a base resolution plan conforming to Section 54K, and such other information as specified\. ## 5\.3 The Base Resolution Plan \(BRP\) - The promoter prepares a BRP conforming to Section 54K and to Section 30\(2\)\. It may be submitted by the CD individually or jointly with another applicant\. - The BRP is the anchor of the pre\-pack: if it does not impair operational creditors’ claims and the CoC approves it, the process can conclude quickly; if it impairs OCs or the CoC is dissatisfied, it is exposed to competition \(see Section 12\)\. # 6\. Appointment and Pre\-Commencement Duties of the RP — Section 54B From the date of approval under Section 54A\(2\)\(e\), and before commencement, the proposed RP must: - Prepare a report in Form P8 confirming whether the CD meets the Section 54A requirements and whether the BRP conforms to Section 54K \(i\.e\. Section 54A\(4\)\(c\)\)\. - File such reports and documents with the Board as specified, and perform such other duties as specified\. These responsibilities cease when the AA admits or rejects the application, or where the CD fails to file the application within 90 days of the directors’ resolution under Section 54A\(2\)\(f\)\. - Fees: the RP’s fees and expenses for this pre\-commencement work are borne by the CD; if PPIRP commences, they form part of the PPIRP process cost \(Regulation 8\)\. - The CD maintains a separate bank account, operated by the IP, for these fees and expenses\. # 7\. Initiation of PPIRP — Section 54C - On satisfying the Section 54A conditions, the CD files the application in Form 1 with the prescribed annexures, in electronic form, with a fee of ₹15,000\. \(Where the electronic facility is unavailable or the data is bulky, submission may be made on a USB device\.\) - Form 1 has three parts: \(i\) details of the applicant and CD; \(ii\) details of the IP; and \(iii\) details of creditors / debt\. - A copy of the application is served on the IBBI — by registered/speed post, by hand or electronically — before filing with the AA\. The application is filed in accordance with the relevant NCLT Rules, 2016\. - The corporate applicant must inform the AA of any winding\-up petition pending against the CD on becoming aware of it\. __2026 change to the documentation requirement — Section 54C\(3\)__ - Earlier, Section 54C\(3\) itself listed the documents to be furnished with the application \(the special resolution, the 66% FC approval, the IP’s consent in Form P1, and a declaration regarding avoidance transactions, among others\)\. - Clause 35 of the IBC \(Amendment\) Act, 2026 substitutes Section 54C\(3\) with an enabling provision: “The corporate applicant shall, along with the application, furnish such information as may be specified\.” The detailed list is thus migrated to the Regulations, giving the IBBI flexibility to revise documentation in light of implementation experience\. - Practical effect: confirm the current document checklist from the latest IBBI \(PPIRP\) Regulations / circular before filing, rather than relying on the older statutory text\. \(An April 2026 discussion paper additionally proposes to drop the avoidance\-transaction declaration at the initiation stage — proposed, not yet notified\.\) - Admission: the AA decides within 14 days — admitting the application if complete, or rejecting it\. Before rejection, 7 days’ time is given to rectify defects\. - The PPIRP commencement date is the date of the AA’s order admitting the application\. Under Section 54D, PPIRP must be completed within 120 days from commencement\. # 8\. Effects of Admission — Sections 54E, 54D and 54G ## 8\.1 On the commencement date \(Section 54E\) - The AA declares a moratorium — Section 14 applies mutatis mutandis\. - The AA appoints the RP named in the application \(or, where disciplinary proceedings are pending against the proposed RP, an RP recommended by the Board\)\. - The RP makes a public announcement within 2 days of commencement \(Form P9\), sending it to every creditor listed in Form P2 and to the information utilities, and publishing it on the websites of the CD \(if any\) and the Board\. ## 8\.2 Information from the CD \(Section 54G\) - Within 2 days of commencement, the CD submits to the RP an updated list of claims \(Form P10\) and a Preliminary Information Memorandum \(PIM\) containing information relevant to formulating a resolution plan\. - Within 2 days of commencement, the CD also submits the Base Resolution Plan to the RP, who presents it to the CoC \(Section 54K\)\. - Misleading information: every director / person who provides a misleading list of claims or PIM is liable to compensate any person who suffers loss as a result\. A person who supplied the information without knowledge of the falsity is not liable; an affected person may seek compensation before the competent court\. ## 8\.3 Timeline discipline \(Section 54D\) - PPIRP is to be completed within 120 days of commencement\. - The RP submits the CoC\-approved resolution plan to the AA within 90 days of commencement\. If the CoC has not approved a plan within 90 days, the RP files, on expiry of that period, an application to terminate the PPIRP\. # 9\. Duties and Powers of the Resolution Professional — Section 54F ## 9\.1 Key duties - Confirm the list of claims \(Form P10\): based on the CD’s records and other material, confirm the details, inform each creditor of its confirmed claim, and invite objections\. - A creditor may file an objection with supporting documents within 7 days of the RP’s communication; the RP may call for further evidence and modify the claim if warranted\. - Maintain and update the list of claims in Form P10; keep it open for inspection by creditors, members, partners, directors and guarantors, display it on the CD’s website \(if any\), file it with the Board, and present it at CoC meetings as updated\. - Where the amount of a claim is not precise, make a best estimate\. Foreign\-currency debt is valued at the exchange rate on the commencement date\. Where a debt is assigned, both the original creditor and the assignee confirm the position to the RP\. - Monitor the management of the CD’s affairs and report any breach to the CoC\. - Constitute the CoC; convene and attend its meetings\. Appoint two registered valuers within 3 days of appointment\. - Prepare the Information Memorandum within 14 days of commencement, on the basis of the PIM and other relevant information\. - Form an opinion and make a determination on avoidance / fraudulent / wrongful\-trading transactions and file the appropriate application with the AA \(by around the 60th day of commencement\)\. ## 9\.2 Powers \(Section 54F\) - Access the books and records of the CD, including those held at information utilities, government authorities or with any other person\. - Attend meetings of the Board / partners\. - Appoint accountants, legal and other professionals; appoint two registered valuers within 3 days\. - Collect information on the CD’s assets, finances, operations and payments for the preceding two years, to assess the financial position and to identify avoidance transactions under Chapter III or VI; prepare a list of assets and liabilities as on the initiation date\. - Financial institutions, employees and the Board of the CD must provide all information and support\. - Fees and expenses are determined as specified; the CoC may impose limits and conditions, and ratifies fees / expenses for the pre\-CoC period\. # 10\. Management of the Corporate Debtor — Sections 54H and 54J - Section 54H: during PPIRP, control of the CD remains with its Board / partners, who must protect and preserve the CD’s value and manage operations as a going concern\. \(This contrasts with CIRP, where control vests in the IRP/RP\.\) - Section 54J: the CoC may, at any time, by a 66% vote, resolve to vest the management of the CD in the RP\. On such a resolution the RP applies to the AA; if the AA is satisfied that management should pass to the RP, it so orders — typically where the management has acted to the detriment of the process\. # 11\. Committee of Creditors — Section 54I ## 11\.1 Constitution and meetings - The RP constitutes the CoC within 7 days of commencement on the basis of the list of claims\. Later updates to the claim list may alter the CoC, but decisions already taken by the existing CoC are not affected by such alterations\. - The first CoC meeting is held within 7 days of constitution\. Section 21 applies \(except sub\-section \(1\)\)\. - Where the CD has only creditors in a class and no unrelated financial creditor, the CoC consists only of the authorised representative\(s\) of the class\. - Where the CD has only operational creditors, the CoC comprises the ten largest OCs, one representative of workmen and one of employees; voting rights are in proportion to the total debt \(OCs \+ workmen \+ employees\)\. - Any change in CoC composition is intimated to all creditors within 2 days\. ## 11\.2 Notice, quorum and conduct - The RP may call a meeting as required; creditors holding 33% of voting rights may require the RP to convene a meeting\. - Notice is given at least 5 days before the meeting; this may be reduced to 24 hours \(48 hours where there are authorised representatives\)\. Notice may be sent by e\-mail \(text or attachment\); the subject line states the CD’s name and the place, date and time of the meeting\. - Quorum: members representing 33% of voting rights, present in person or by video / audio\-visual means; the CoC may modify the quorum for future meetings\. - Adjournment: to the same time and place on the next day, and the adjourned meeting is quorate with the members attending it\. - The RP chairs the meeting and ensures the required quorum is maintained throughout\. ## 11\.3 Where there are creditors in a class - The RP provides each authorised representative \(AR\) with the list of creditors in the class within 3 days of commencement, and updates it as required\. The AR has no role in receipt or confirmation of claims\. - The RP provides electronic means of communication between the AR and the creditors in the class\. - The voting share of a creditor in a class is proportionate to the financial debt, including interest at 8% per annum unless a different rate is agreed\. - The AR circulates the agenda and may seek preliminary views: creditors have at least a 12\-hour window, opening at least 24 hours after the AR seeks views; preliminary views are not voting instructions\. - Post\-meeting: the RP circulates the minutes electronically within 24 hours and seeks the vote of members who did not vote, keeping electronic voting open for at least 24 hours from circulation of the minutes\. The AR then circulates the minutes to the class, announces the voting window at least 24 hours before it opens, and keeps it open at least 12 hours\. # 12\. Consideration of the Base Resolution Plan and Competing Plans — Section 54K - The CD submits the BRP to the RP within 2 days of commencement; the RP presents it to the CoC\. The CoC may give the CD an opportunity to revise the BRP before approving it or before inviting competing plans\. Section 30 applies to the submission of resolution plans\. - If the BRP does not impair any operational\-creditor claims, the CoC may approve it for submission to the AA\. - If the CoC does not approve the BRP — because it impairs OC claims or for any other reason — the RP invites prospective resolution applicants to submit competing plans, publishing brief particulars of the invitation in Form P11 not later than 21 days from commencement\. The RP provides the evaluation matrix and information to prospective applicants as approved by the CoC\. - On receipt, the RP confirms whether each plan meets Section 30\(2\) and presents conforming plans to the CoC, which selects one\. The selected plan competes with the BRP\. - Under the 25\-02\-2026 amendment, a competing plan prevails over the BRP where it is “significantly better” \(as scored on the evaluation matrix\)\. The finalised plan is approved by the CoC by a 66% vote, and the RP applies to the AA with the CoC\-approved plan\. - If the CoC approves no plan, the RP applies to the AA to terminate PPIRP\. Where the BRP is approved with impairment of OCs, the CoC may require the promoters to dilute their shareholding; reasons for rejecting a plan are recorded by the CoC\. *Note: “impairment” of OC claims means a reduction of their confirmed claims\.* # 13\. Approval or Rejection by the Adjudicating Authority — Sections 54L and 54M - If the plan conforms to Section 30\(2\) and provides for its effective implementation, the AA approves it by order \(the framework contemplates approval within about 30 days\)\. - An approved plan binds all stakeholders; the moratorium ceases; and the RP forwards the records of the PPIRP to the Board for its database\. - If the plan does not satisfy the conditions, the AA rejects it and passes an order of termination under Section 54N\. - Appeal: an appeal against an order under Section 54L lies under Section 61\(3\) \(Section 54M\)\. # 14\. Termination and Conversion — Section 54N - On an order of termination under Section 54N, the AA may pass a liquidation order under Section 33; the PPIRP cost forms part of the liquidation cost\. - The CoC may terminate PPIRP at any time by a 66% vote; the cost of PPIRP is borne by the CD\. - Conversion to CIRP: the CoC may, by a 66% vote, resolve to terminate PPIRP and initiate CIRP under Chapter II, provided the CD is eligible\. On such a resolution, the RP applies to the AA, which, within 30 days, terminates PPIRP and orders that the process proceed as CIRP\. That order is treated as an order under Section 7, appoints the RP \(subject to written consent and the prescribed conditions\), and declares that the PPIRP cost forms part of the CIRP cost\. The CIRP commencement date is the date of that order\. # 15\.
